changedPattern.equivalenceArgument: A local part cannot contain '@', so from any start inside a maximal [A-Za-z0-9._%+-] run the local part extends to the same run end and the rest of the match is identical. A start inside a run therefore succeeds exactly when the earliest start in that run succeeds. The old engine's leftmost start inside a run is either the run start (allowed by the lookbehind) or, after a previous match, the previous match end (allowed by \G). Possessive ++ only drops backtracking into shorter local parts, and a shorter local part is always followed by a local-class character, not '@'. No empty match is possible.
